findings.quote_english: Customer data at rest are stored continuously and exclusively in the territory of EU member states and EFTA member states.
findings.value: partial
findings.title: Vyhláška č. 505/2025 Sb., o některých požadavcích pro zápis do katalogu cloud computingu (znění od 2026-01-01)
findings.publisher: Ministerstvo vnitra ČR – e-Sbírka (official Collection of Laws portal)
findings.note: This is the official text of the NÚKIB cloud-catalogue decree, served as JSON by the official e-Sbírka text API because the HTML page is a JavaScript app. Annex 3 (high level) requires storage in the EU/EFTA and Annex 4 (critical level) requires processing in the Czech Republic; the rule covers only cloud at the higher levels, so the value is partial.

review.reason: Decree 505/2025 is a binding regulation that requires customer data at rest to be stored only in EU and EFTA states, but it applies only to cloud services at the 'vysoká' (high) security level, covers storage at rest rather than processing, and counts EFTA as well as the EU.

findings.question: Is a cloud certification that requires immunity from non-EU law in force or adopted for government use? yes = In force and required for sensitive government workloads; partial = Adopted or in force but not required; no = A source states no such certification exists or applies
findings.quote: Poskytovatel v případě, že obdrží žádost cizozemských orgánů o zpřístupnění nebo předání zákaznických dat nebo specifických provozních údajů, tuto žádost odmítne a data nevydá a nezpřístupní.
findings.quote_english: If the provider receives a request from foreign authorities to disclose or hand over customer data or specific operational data, it refuses the request and does not release or disclose the data.
findings.value: yes
findings.title: Vyhláška č. 505/2025 Sb., o některých požadavcích pro zápis do katalogu cloud computingu (znění od 2026-01-01)
findings.publisher: Ministerstvo vnitra ČR – e-Sbírka (official Collection of Laws portal)
findings.note: This is Annex 4 (security level 'kritická') of the binding decree for entry in the government cloud catalogue; Act 365/2000 Sb. lets public bodies use only catalogue-listed cloud at the level their assessment requires, so refusing foreign access is mandatory for critical workloads (e-Sbírka JSON text API).

review.reason: Decree 505/2025 is in force and requires that a provider in the 'vysoká' security level of the public-administration cloud catalogue refuse foreign authorities' requests for customer data; the quote does not say whether public authorities must use such services, so 'partial' would also be arguable.
